text:
7. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
7.1. The device must be industrial type and resistant to severe environmental conditions. In order to guarantee this durability of the device, it must have the following certificates and test reports related to them must be submitted to the relevant institution when necessary.
- IEC 61000-4-2 (ESD)
- IEC 61000-4-3 (RS)
- IEC 61000-4-4 (EFT)
- IEC 61000-4-5 (Surge)
- IEC 61000-4-6 (CS)
- EN 55032: 2012/AC: 2013 (CE & RE) Class B
ACCEPTED
7.2. If the certificates in Article 2.4 cannot be provided, it must be guaranteed by the company that the device is of industrial type and is resistant to severe environmental conditions, has the necessary protections so that it will not fail under conditions such as lightning strikes, energy problems, etc. and all malfunctions occurring in the product must be eliminated under warranty.
ACCEPTED
7.3. The device to be offered shall have 4/6/8 copper ethernet ports that can operate at 10/100/1000Mbps speeds. In addition, there will be at least 2 SFP module slots on the device to support 1 / 2.5 Gbps speeds.
ACCEPTED
7.4.
7.5. 1 1000 Base-LX SFP module produced by the manufacturer (it shall be proved with the production documents that it is not OEM) may be requested by TT together with the device. The price of the requested module will be specified in the offer price list.
ACCEPTED
7.6. The Industrial Switch shall have at least 4/6/8 (two/four/eight) 10/100/1000Base-T/TX RJ45 autosense MDI/MDI-x ports and at least 2 (two) 100/1000/2500MbpsBaseSFP ports. 1000Base-SX, 1000Base-LX, 1000Base-T/T/TX, 2.5GBase-SX and 2.5GBase-LX modules can be installed to SFP ports. The transceiver modules to be supplied will be original modules produced by the Industrial Switch manufacturer. OEM modules will not be accepted.
ACCEPTED
7.7. The Industrial Switch shall have at least 512 (five hundred twelve) MB RAM and at least 128 (one hundred twenty eight) MB flash memory.
ACCEPTED
7.8. At least 16000 (sixteen thousand) MAC addresses shall be supported.
ACCEPTED
7.9. Industrial Switch shall include overcurrent and overvoltage protection circuit.
ACCEPTED
7.10. Industrial Switch shall have an all-metal external enclosure in IP40 standards.
ACCEPTED
7.11. Industrial Switch must have the necessary apparatus to be mounted on a 19 inch rack cabinet.
ACCEPTED
7.12. All ports on the Industrial Switch will be able to operate at the same time without congestion and at cable speed.
ACCEPTED
7.13. Industrial Switch shall support IEEE 802.1q VLAN protocol. It shall support at least 256 (two hundred and fifty-six) active VLANs and 4000 (four thousand) VLAN IDs.
ACCEPTED
7.14. The Industrial Switch shall support IEEE 802.1D mac bridging standards. It shall also support 802.1s MST protocol to prevent loops on different subnets, independently, and 802.1w protocol for fast convergence.
ACCEPTED
7.15. The device must support RING protocol. Traffic flow transition over the redundant link should be under 20ms (twenty milliseconds).
ACCEPTED
7.16. Industrial Switch shall support 802.3ad protocol and shall be able to group at least 8 (eight) ports with the same feature (port-channel).
ACCEPTED
7.17. Industrial Switch should support Jumbo Frame up to 10K size.
ACCEPTED
7.18. DHCP scopes should be defined on the Industrial Switch and it should be able to send IP address and other necessary information to end devices.
ACCEPTED
7.19. Industrial Switch should provide 802.1ab Link Layer Discovery Protocol support for the detection of other devices connected to it. Thus, it will be able to collect information about its neighboring devices and transmit information about itself to its neighbors.
ACCEPTED
7.20. Industrial Switch will be sent to the sites configured with the configurations previously given by Türk Telekom.
ACCEPTED
7.21. Industrial Switch should support quality of service configuration. For each port, there should be speed limiting in the direction of incoming traffic and traffic shaping in the direction of outgoing traffic, 8 hardware queues, weighted and strict prioritization support, DSCP, 802.1p Class of service, ToS based, classification and re-marking, congestion avoidance algorithm service features.
ACCEPTED
7.22. Industrial Switch shall be able to take at least Dynamic ARP Inspection or Dynamic ARP Protection, DHCP Snooping, Management ACL, L2/L3/L4 Access Control Lists, Ip Source Guard security measures or support related protocols in order to ensure layer 2 security.
ACCEPTED
7.23. Industrial Switch shall support static routing and routing between defined vlan interfaces.
ACCEPTED
7.24. Port mirroring support shall be available. Multiple source ports can be mirrored to the destination port.
ACCEPTED
7.25. Industrial Switch should support SNMP v3, HTTPS SSHv2 and sFTP features for management purposes.
ACCEPTED
7.26. All necessary configurations should be possible from the Industrial Switch HTTPS based web interface. In addition, this web interface should have Turkish language support.
ACCEPTED
7.27. Industrial Switch firmware updates can be updated via sFTP protocol with the current firmware file in the file extension of the server previously written in it.
ACCEPTED
7.28. The events and alarms that occur on the Industrial Switch can be sent to external systems using SNMP Trap and syslog protocols. Events and alarms should also be queried periodically by SNMP get. In addition, using one of the sflow protocols, it will be able to sample traffic and send these samples to external systems.
ACCEPTED
7.29. Devices shall have a console port. All functions of the device can be done through the command line accessible via console or SSHv2.
ACCEPTED
7.30. The device shall be able to authenticate for management purposes from a central authentication server using TACACS or Radius protocol.
ACCEPTED
7.31. Industrial Switches must be able to provide an external management platform upon request. The management platform should provide at least 250 devices without requiring additional licenses.
ACCEPTED
7.32. If requested, the management platform should be able to monitor different branded Industrial Switches operating in the existing structure in detail. No additional cost should be charged for this feature.
ACCEPTED
7.33. If requested, the management platform should be capable of displaying all status, vlan information, connected user and mac address information, graphical representation of traffic passing through the interfaces, temperature and processor usage of devices and neighboring device information of different brand devices, as a minimum.
ACCEPTED
